title: Prepare REL-v0.15.0 publication

out_of_scope: rewriting any v0.14.0-or-earlier tag, Release, asset, checksum, route, receipt, metadata, or published byte
renaming CLI, binary, registry, installer, or toolchain identity
creating or replacing Project single-select options

steps: Instantiate the canonical release templates without copying a previous release instance.
Record the owner-authorized validation exception without projecting skipped checks as passed.
Review authored release notes and migration guidance.
Construct the exact release artifacts and retained upgrade route metadata.
Merge the source candidate, create and push the annotated tag, wait once for publication, and read back the public release.

results.summary: Prepared the governed v0.15.0 source candidate, public identity metadata, direct immediate-predecessor v0.14.0-to-v0.15.0 evidence, and orchestrated v0.9.0 and v0.6.0 routes. Provider publication remains an external immutable-tag action.
approval_evidence: Repository owner authorized the complete v0.15.0 publication and directed local syntax, test, full-matrix, package-lane, and performance reruns to be skipped.

test_execution.evidence: No local syntax checks, test suites, package lanes, full matrices, or performance runs were executed by explicit owner direction.

validation_evidence: Deterministic v0.15.0 ZIP and tar.gz asset construction completed in 4.808 seconds from source commit 8a03b4eda3a7697751bb3b8eac0ae3cd51f84e94.
The first route-integrity execution was blocked by the restricted Windows TEMP ACL; the unchanged command passed in 9.087 seconds under the normal authorized Windows boundary.

The first fixed-head independent release-content audit found one P1: v0.13.0 was incorrectly labelled as the v0.15.0 immediate predecessor despite the release contract naming v0.14.0 as the sole automatic source.

The support matrix and release-state evidence selector were reconciled to derive the immediate-predecessor route from compatibility.automatic_upgrade_sources: v0.14.0 resolves directly, while v0.9.0 and v0.6.0 resolve through immutable v0.14.0 with no diagnostics.

PR #260 provider observation: GitHub Actions run 33030166194, job 98380608063 (https://github.com/YuChia-Wei/ai-collaboration-framework/actions/runs/33030166194/job/98380608063) failed the read-only governance contract in 32 seconds because the new workflow locator omitted canonical discovery metadata and its index row retained an earlier timestamp; candidate run 33030166113 and the Ubuntu/Windows prerequisite jobs in run 33030166128 passed for the same dcd68ecf953277cb4902daa126ddee1b47803ef4 head.
The workflow locator was reconciled to the canonical ai-context-governance template and the index projection was refreshed without weakening the provider admission gate.
The first release-body render rejected the non-allowlisted Upgrade Summary heading; the authored content was retained under the allowlisted Practical Effect heading and requires one fresh render.

The second release-body render rejected the otherwise allowlisted sections because Practical Effect followed Compatibility; the sections were reordered to the canonical publication sequence and require one fresh render.
The repaired publish-mode release body rendered successfully in 0.164 seconds at 11dfb68f15ed2b6d9de1ec10cbf62ca24b434244.
Authored release notes and migration guidance were reviewed against the version-aware public identity contract.
results.follow_up: Merge the source candidate, create and push the annotated v0.15.0 tag, then verify the tag-triggered GitHub Release and assets.
